scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Baum-Welch is $\mathrm{EM}$: the $\mathrm{E}$ step computes expected counts, the $\mathrm{M}$ step re-estimates from their ratios

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: the left is one iteration loop (current model → $\mathrm{E}$ step → expected counts → $\mathrm{M}$ step → new model, then back); below, $\xi$ is split into four parts; the right gives three re-estimation formulas.

scene-u01-pnew1-36.name: text#36
scene-u01-pnew1-36.text: Set $\mathcal{S}=\overline{\mathcal{S}}$ and repeat; stop when the gain is at most $\epsilon$

scene-u01-pnew1-54.name: text#54
scene-u01-pnew1-54.text: The $\mathrm{E}$ step takes expectations over hidden states; the $\mathrm{M}$ step re-estimates, maximizing the expected log-likelihood.

scene-u01-pnew1-69.name: text#69
scene-u01-pnew1-69.text: Numerators are expected counts, denominators totals; the emission numerator only sums steps where the observation is $r$

scene-u01-pnew1-71.name: text#71
scene-u01-pnew1-71.text: $\xi$ and flow from source; numbers by code

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: One re-estimation lifts the likelihood from $0.050836$ to $0.105207$

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left is the $\mathrm{E}$ step (four terms of $\xi_1$ and expected transition counts summed over three steps); the right shows five parameters before (gray) and after (green) the $\mathrm{M}$ step.

scene-u01-pnew2-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew2-8.text: $\mathrm{E}$ step: from $\xi$ to expected transition counts

scene-u01-pnew2-46.name: text#46
scene-u01-pnew2-46.text: The total is the expected number of transitions leaving that coin, the denominator for transition re-estimation.

scene-u01-pnew2-79.name: text#79
scene-u01-pnew2-79.text: $P(X\mid\mathcal{S})=0.050836\to P(X\mid\overline{\mathcal{S}})=0.105207$; with only $4$ observations the parameters move far ($P_2(H)$ jumps from $0.2$ to $0.6307$), a sign of overfitting.

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: From both starts the likelihood only rises and ends at the same value; but $\mathrm{EM}$ only guarantees no worsening

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left shows likelihood over $30$ iterations (log scale, blue: good start, orange: poor start, dashed: final value); the right lists four practical limits.

scene-u01-pnew3-39.name: text#39
scene-u01-pnew3-39.text: From $6.1\times10^{-5}$ up to the same value

scene-u01-pnew3-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew3-45.text: "Baum-Welch finds the best model" is wrong: $\mathrm{EM}$ only keeps the likelihood from dropping and may stop at a local maximum.

scene-u01-pnew3-49.name: text#49
scene-u01-pnew3-49.text: $\alpha$, $\beta$ are products of probabilities and underflow over many steps; one shared set of scale factors cancels in the product.

scene-u01-pnew3-53.name: text#53
scene-u01-pnew3-53.text: Set forbidden transitions to $0$: the re-estimation numerator is $0$, so the zero persists.

scene-u01-pnew3-57.name: text#57
scene-u01-pnew3-57.text: Sequences must be long or many enough for every transition to appear often; otherwise parameters are unstable.
